core_meaning.primary_meaning: Aasimah corresponds to the Arabic form عاصمة and is glossed in this record as “Protector, guardian, keeper.” The record associates the form with root ع ص م (ʿ-ṣ-m). The record identifies the form as feminine. The lexical gloss describes the word-form; Qur’anic occurrence, religious recommendation, popularity, and a name-bearer’s character are separate claims and are not established by this gloss alone.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Aasimah corresponds to the Arabic form عاصمة (Arabic root ع ص م (ʿ-ṣ-m); عَاصِمَة (ʿāṣimah)). Its core sense is protector, guardian; keeper. Aasimah is Arabic عَاصِمَة (ʿāṣimah) 'Protector, guardian, keeper', the feminine active participle (fāʿilah pattern, feminine of عاصم (ʿāṣim)) of عَصَمَ (ʿaṣama, 'to protect, to preserve') from the root ع ص م (ʿ-ṣ-m). Aasimah is a variant romanization of Aasima.

etymology.morphology: Feminine active participle (fāʿilah pattern, feminine of عاصم) of عَصَمَ, built on the root ع ص م.
etymology.etymological_meaning: From the root ع ص م (ʿ-ṣ-m)
etymology.etymology_explanation: The form عاصمة is an established Arabic lexical item — the feminine of عاصم (ʿāṣim) — and Aasimah is the word itself used as a personal name rather than a derived or diminutive form.
